Atomic Annie was an American towed artillery piece capable of firing a nuclear device. It weighed 83 tons, was 84 feet long and 16 feet wide. It was transported by two specially designed tractors capable of independent steering in the manner of some extra-long fire engines.

This image is from the first and only test of a nuclear shell fired from Atomic Annie. The detonation occurred 19 seconds after its firing and detonated over 10 km (6.25 mi) away from the gun. The explosion was an air burst 160 m (524 ft) above the ground with an estimated yield of 15 kilotons, around the same level as Little Boy, the bomb dropped on Hiroshima.

After the successful test, there were at least 20 of the cannons manufactured at a cost of $800,000 each. They were deployed to Europe and South Korea, often shifted around to avoid being detected and targeted by opposing forces. Due to the size of the apparatus, their limited range, the development of nuclear shells compatible with existing artillery pieces and the development of rocket and missile based nuclear artillery, the M65 was effectively obsolete soon after it was deployed. However, it remained a prestige weapon and was not retired until 1963.
